title: Why Ahimaaz Wanted to Run Even Without Good News
paragraphs: Why Ahimaaz Wanted to Run Even Without Good News
There are moments in Scripture that feel painfully human.
Not polished. Not heroic. Not victorious.
Just painfully… human.
One of those moments lives inside 2 Samuel 18.
A battlefield still wet with blood. A father waiting at the gate. A kingdom fractured by betrayal. A son hanging dead beneath a tree. And in the middle of all of it…
A man named Ahimaaz desperately begging for permission to run.
But there was one problem.
He had no good news.
And somehow, that sounds exactly like many believers today.
Running fast. Posting constantly. Speaking loudly. Moving publicly. Being seen. Being noticed. Being active. Being involved.
Yet carrying no real message from God.
This story is deeper than most people realize. Because Ahimaaz was not evil. He was not rebellious. He was not wicked.
He simply wanted the platform before he carried the burden.
And that danger still exists today.
The Story Most People Read Too Quickly
The context of this moment is devastating.
Absalom, David’s son, had rebelled against his own father. He stole the hearts of Israel. He attempted to overthrow the kingdom. Civil war erupted.
David loved his son deeply despite Absalom’s betrayal.
Before the battle even began, David gave one emotional command:
“Deal gently for my sake with the young man Absalom.”
(2 Samuel 18:5)
But Absalom died anyway.
Joab ignored David’s heart.
The rebellion was crushed. But the victory felt like a funeral.
Then came the question:
Who will carry the news to the king?
Joab chose a Cushite messenger.
But Ahimaaz suddenly interrupted the moment.
Scripture says:
“Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the LORD hath avenged him of his enemies.”
— 2 Samuel 18:19
The Hebrew wording is deeply revealing.
The phrase “bear tidings” comes from the Hebrew root בָּשַׂר (basar).
This word means:
• to announce news • to proclaim glad tidings • to bring a message of victory • to declare good news
This same root eventually becomes connected to the concept of gospel proclamation.
But here is the tragedy.
Ahimaaz wanted to carry “good news” in a moment where the king would not experience it as good news.
Because heaven’s victory can still feel devastating to a wounded heart.
Joab understood something Ahimaaz did not.
This was not a moment for excitement.
This was a moment requiring emotional weight.
Joab answered:
“Thou shalt not bear tidings this day…”
— 2 Samuel 18:20
In Hebrew:
לֹא־אִישׁ בְּשֹׂרָה אַתָּה הַיּוֹם
Transliteration: Lo ish besorah attah hayom.
Literal sense:
“You are not a man of news today.”
That line hits hard.
Because some people are called to speak in one season but not another.
Not every messenger is prepared for every assignment.
Sometimes zeal outruns maturity.
Sometimes passion outruns wisdom.
Sometimes ambition outruns discernment.
And sometimes people want to run because being seen feels more rewarding than carrying truth.
Ahimaaz Was Fast… But Empty
What happens next is one of the most overlooked warnings in the Bible.
Ahimaaz keeps insisting.
He begs to run.
Again. And again.
Finally Joab says:
“Run.”
And Ahimaaz outruns the Cushite.
He arrives first.
Imagine the scene.
David is trembling between hope and dread.
The watchman sees someone running.
Then another.
The king says:
“If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth.”
(2 Samuel 18:25)
The anticipation builds.
Ahimaaz finally arrives.
And what does he say?
“All is well.”
But it was not well.
Not for David.
Not emotionally. Not spiritually. Not relationally.
Then David asks the question that mattered most:
“Is the young man Absalom safe?”
(2 Samuel 18:29)
And suddenly Ahimaaz collapses under the weight of the assignment he begged to carry.
He answers:
“When Joab sent the king’s servant, and me thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what it was.”
This is astonishing.
He ran passionately. He arrived first. He looked impressive. He sounded confident.
But when the moment demanded truth…
He had nothing.
That should terrify every preacher. Every content creator. Every ministry leader. Every influencer. Every believer chasing visibility.
Because speed is not the same thing as substance.
Being first is not the same thing as being faithful.
Having an audience is not the same thing as carrying revelation.
Many people today are spiritually sprinting with empty hands.
And deep down… they know it.
The Difference Between Ahimaaz and the Cushite
The Cushite was slower.
Less celebrated. Less emotionally driven. Less eager for recognition.
But he carried the actual message.
He delivered the painful truth faithfully.
Sometimes the Kingdom is advanced more by faithful obedience than visible charisma.
The modern world rewards Ahimaaz.
Fast. Visible. Energetic. Impressive.
But heaven still values truth carriers.
The Greek language of the New Testament later captures this beautifully.
The word for gospel is:
εὐαγγέλιον (euangelion)
Meaning:
“good news” “glad tidings” “a message worth announcing”
But biblical good news was never about making people feel temporarily inspired.
It was about truth.
Even costly truth.
Even convicting truth.
Even truth that pierced hearts before healing them.
Paul told Timothy:
“Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.”
— 2 Timothy 4:2
The Greek phrase “preach the word” is:
κήρυξον τὸν λόγον
(Kēruxon ton logon)
“Kēruxon” comes from κηρύσσω (kēryssō).
It means:
• to herald publicly • to proclaim with authority • to announce as an official messenger
A herald did not invent the message.
He carried the king’s message accurately.
That is the difference.
Ahimaaz wanted the run. The Cushite carried the burden.
One wanted movement. The other carried truth.
And modern Christianity is filled with people addicted to movement.
Posting. Talking. Uploading. Streaming. Performing. Reacting. Chasing relevance.
But God is still asking:
“Who actually carries My message?”
The Hidden Sin Nobody Talks About
Ahimaaz reveals something uncomfortable about the human heart.
Sometimes people want proximity to spiritual importance more than surrender to spiritual responsibility.
They want to feel involved.
They want visibility.
They want significance.
But they have not yet developed the weight required to carry truth through emotionally difficult moments.
That is why some believers disappear the moment ministry becomes painful.
The moment truth costs relationships. The moment obedience becomes lonely. The moment following Jesus stops feeling exciting.
Jesus never called people to perform spirituality.
He called them to die.
The Greek word for disciple is μαθητής (mathētēs).
Meaning:
• learner • follower • disciplined student
Not celebrity. Not personality. Not platform builder.
Follower.
Modern culture says:
“Build your audience.”
Jesus says:
“Carry your cross.”
Those are not the same mission.
And maybe this article hurts because some people recognize themselves in Ahimaaz.
Still running. Still exhausted. Still striving. Still posting. Still trying to prove they matter.
Yet secretly empty.
Secretly afraid that if someone finally asks the deeper question…
There will be no answer.
This Is Why Intimacy With God Matters More Than Visibility
The danger of public Christianity without private surrender is catastrophic.
Because eventually every runner reaches a moment where the king asks:
“What is the real condition?”
And charisma cannot answer that.
Only truth can.
Only intimacy can.
Only genuine relationship with God can sustain the weight of real ministry.
In John 15, Jesus said:
“I am the vine, ye are the branches.”
The Greek word for “abide” used repeatedly in this chapter is μένω (menō).
Meaning:
• remain • dwell • stay connected • continue intimately
Fruit does not come from frantic movement.
It comes from remaining connected to Christ.
Many believers are burning out because they are running faster than they are abiding.
Faster than they are praying. Faster than they are repenting. Faster than they are healing. Faster than they are listening.
And eventually the soul collapses under spiritual emptiness.
This article is not attacking passionate people.
Passion matters.
But passion without truth becomes noise.
Passion without surrender becomes performance.
Passion without intimacy becomes exhaustion.
God Is More Concerned About Faithfulness Than Visibility
One of the saddest realities in modern Christianity is how deeply people crave recognition.
Even spiritually.
Especially spiritually.
But Scripture repeatedly shows that God often works most deeply in hidden places.
David was hidden in fields. Moses was hidden in Midian. Elijah was hidden by the brook. John the Baptist lived in wilderness. Jesus spent thirty hidden years before three years of ministry.
Hiddenness is not punishment.
Sometimes it is preparation.
Ahimaaz wanted acceleration.
But spiritual weight takes time.
The Hebrew concept of glory helps explain this.
The Hebrew word כָּבוֹד (kavod) literally carries the idea of:
• heaviness • weight • substance • honor with gravity
Real spiritual authority carries weight.
Not theatrics. Not hype. Not performance.
Weight.
And weight is developed in hidden obedience.
Not public excitement.
Some of you reading this are frustrated because your life feels unseen.
You feel forgotten. Delayed. Overlooked.
But maybe God is protecting you from running ahead of your maturity.
Maybe heaven loves you too much to hand you a microphone before your character can survive it.
Maybe the silence is mercy.
Maybe the delay is protection.
Maybe God would rather develop depth inside you than speed around you.
And honestly…
That realization changes everything.
The Gospel Is Not About Looking Alive While Dying Inside
One reason this story hits so deeply is because many people know what it feels like to look spiritually active while internally exhausted.
Smiling publicly. Breaking privately.
Quoting Scripture publicly. Questioning everything privately.
Serving publicly. Bleeding privately.
But Jesus did not come merely to create religious runners.
He came to resurrect dead hearts.
The Gospel is not behavior modification.
It is transformation.
The Greek word μετανοέω (metanoeō), translated “repent,” means:
• to change the mind • to turn inwardly • to undergo spiritual transformation
Real Christianity is not cosmetic.
It is crucifixion followed by resurrection.
And maybe some people reading this are tired.
Not physically.
Spiritually.
Tired of pretending. Tired of performing. Tired of running. Tired of looking okay.
This is your reminder:
Jesus never asked you to impress Him.
He asked you to follow Him.
And there is mercy even for exhausted runners.
Peter failed publicly. Thomas doubted openly. Jonah ran away. David collapsed morally.
Yet grace still pursued them.
That is the beauty of the Gospel.
Jesus does not merely expose empty people.
He restores them.
And maybe that is why this story lingers.
Because deep down, many people know what it feels like to outrun their own soul.
To move externally while dying internally.
To crave purpose while lacking peace.
To chase calling while neglecting communion with God.
But Jesus still stands calling weary people back to Himself.
Not into performance.
Into relationship.
Into truth.
Into surrender.
Into rest.
Maybe You Needed This More Than You Realize
Maybe this article exposed something hidden.
Maybe you have been running because slowing down would force you to confront what is actually happening inside your heart.
Maybe you have been terrified that if you stop moving… the pain will finally catch up.
But healing cannot happen in nonstop noise.
Sometimes God allows exhaustion because exhaustion finally breaks self-reliance.
Sometimes the collapse becomes the doorway to honesty.
And honesty is where healing begins.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
Some people are smiling publicly while collapsing privately.
They need this reminder.
Some people are not exhausted because they have done too little.
They are exhausted because they have been running without carrying what only intimacy with Jesus can provide.
Filipino Version:
Bakit Gustong Tumakbo ni Ahimaaz Kahit Wala Siyang Magandang Balita
May mga bahagi sa Biblia na sobrang tao.
Hindi perpekto. Hindi makintab. Hindi parang pelikulang laging panalo.
Kundi sugatan. Mabigat. At totoo.
Isa sa mga tagpong iyon ay nasa 2 Samuel 18.
Isang digmaan na amoy dugo pa. Isang amang naghihintay sa tarangkahan. Isang kahariang nabiyak dahil sa pagtataksil. Isang anak na nakabitin nang patay sa puno.
At sa gitna ng lahat…
May isang lalaking desperadong gustong tumakbo.
Ang pangalan niya ay Ahimaaz.
Pero may problema.
Wala siyang magandang balita.
At kung tutuusin…
Maraming Kristiyano ngayon ang kamukha niya.
Laging gumagalaw. Laging may post. Laging may opinyon. Laging visible. Laging active. Laging gustong mapansin.
Pero walang tunay na dala mula sa presensya ng Diyos.
Mas malalim ang kuwentong ito kaysa sa inaakala ng karamihan.
Hindi masamang tao si Ahimaaz. Hindi siya rebelde. Hindi siya traydor.
Gusto lang niyang tumakbo bago niya talaga madala ang bigat ng mensahe.
At hanggang ngayon… nangyayari pa rin iyon.
Maraming gustong maging visible bago maging broken. Maraming gustong mangaral bago matutong sumunod. Maraming gustong mag-minister pero ayaw munang magpahubog.
At iyan ang delikado.
Ang Konteksto na Masyadong Minamadali ng Marami
Si Absalom, anak ni David, ay naghimagsik laban sa sarili niyang ama.
Inagaw niya ang puso ng Israel. Sinubukan niyang kunin ang trono. At sumabog ang digmaang sibil.
Pero kahit ganoon… mahal pa rin siya ni David.
Bago magsimula ang laban, sinabi ni David:
“Deal gently for my sake with the young man Absalom.”
(2 Samuel 18:5)
Pero namatay pa rin si Absalom.
Nanalo ang hukbo. Pero para kay David… parang wala ring panalo.
Pagkatapos ng digmaan, kailangang may magdala ng balita.
Pinili ni Joab ang Cushite messenger.
Pero biglang sumingit si Ahimaaz.
Sabi ng Kasulatan:
“Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings…”
— 2 Samuel 18:19
Ang salitang “bear tidings” ay mula sa Hebrew na:
בָּשַׂר (basar)
Na ang ibig sabihin ay:
• magdala ng balita • magpahayag ng good news • mag-anunsyo ng tagumpay
Ito rin ang ugat ng konsepto ng “gospel” o mabuting balita.
Pero narito ang masakit.
Para kay Ahimaaz, magandang balita iyon.
Pero para kay David?
Patay ang anak niya.
Minsan kahit may panalo… masakit pa rin.
Naiintindihan iyon ni Joab.
Hindi ito oras para maging excited.
Ito ay oras na nangangailangan ng bigat.
Kaya sinabi niya:
“Thou shalt not bear tidings this day…”
Sa Hebrew:
לֹא־אִישׁ בְּשֹׂרָה אַתָּה הַיּוֹם
Lo ish besorah attah hayom.
Literal:
“Hindi ikaw ang taong dapat magdala ng balita ngayong araw.”
Napakalalim niyan.
Dahil hindi lahat ng masigasig ay handa.
Minsan nauuna ang excitement kaysa maturity. Minsan nauuna ang passion kaysa wisdom. Minsan nauuna ang ambition kaysa tunay na calling.
At minsan… gusto lang ng tao na mapansin.
Mabilis si Ahimaaz… Pero Walang Dalang Totoong Mensahe
Hindi tumigil si Ahimaaz.
Paulit-ulit siyang nagpilit.
Hanggang sa sinabi ni Joab:
“Sige. Tumakbo ka.”
At inunahan nga niya ang Cushite.
Siya ang unang dumating.
Isipin mo ang eksena.
Naghihintay si David. Kinakabahan. Umaasa. Natatakot.
Pagdating ni Ahimaaz, sinabi niya:
“All is well.”
Pero hindi naman talaga.
Hindi okay si David. Hindi okay ang puso niya. Hindi okay ang pamilya niya.
Pagkatapos tinanong ni David ang pinakamahalagang tanong:
“Ligtas ba si Absalom?”
At doon bumigay si Ahimaaz.
Hindi niya masagot.
Bigla niyang sinabi na hindi niya alam.
Napakasakit niyan.
Tumakbo siya. Mukhang confident. Mukhang passionate. Mukhang ready.
Pero nang kailangan na ng totoong sagot…
Wala siyang maibigay.
At kung tutuusin…
Maraming tao ngayon ang ganiyan.
Maingay online. Visible sa ministry. Active sa church. Laging may sinasabi.
Pero kapag tinanong mo:
“Kumusta talaga ang kaluluwa mo?”
Tahimik.
Dahil ang bilis ay hindi kapalit ng lalim.
Ang pagiging visible ay hindi kapalit ng intimacy kay God.
At ang audience ay hindi awtomatikong katumbas ng anointing.
Ang Kaibahan ni Ahimaaz at ng Cushite
Mas mabagal ang Cushite. Hindi siya flashy. Hindi siya dramatic.
Pero dala niya ang totoong mensahe.
Minsan mas ginagamit ng Diyos ang faithful kaysa famous.
Pero ang problema ngayon…
Mas gusto ng mundo ang mabilis.
Mas gusto ang viral. Mas gusto ang trending. Mas gusto ang performance.
Pero sa langit…
Truth still matters.
Sa Greek, ang salitang “gospel” ay:
εὐαγγέλιον (euangelion)
Ibig sabihin:
“mabuting balita.”
Pero ang tunay na mabuting balita ay hindi simpleng motivational speech.
Ito ay katotohanan.
Kahit minsan masakit. Kahit minsan nakaka-convict. Kahit minsan umiiyak ka habang naririnig mo.
Hindi tinawag ng Diyos ang mga tao para mag-perform.
Tinawag Niya silang mamatay sa sarili.
Ang salitang disciple sa Greek ay:
μαθητής (mathētēs)
Ibig sabihin:
• estudyante • tagasunod • disiplinadong learner
Hindi celebrity. Hindi influencer. Hindi performer.
Follower.
Sinasabi ng mundo:
“Build your platform.”
Sinasabi ni Jesus:
“Pasanin mo ang krus mo.”
Magkaibang landas iyon.
At baka kaya masakit itong basahin…
Dahil may mga nakakakita ng sarili nila kay Ahimaaz.
Pagod na. Pero tuloy pa rin sa takbo.
Visible. Pero empty.
Active. Pero disconnected kay God.
Bakit Mas Mahalaga ang Intimacy Kaysa Visibility
Darating ang punto na tatanungin ka rin ng Hari:
“Ano talaga ang kondisyon?”
At hindi sasagot diyan ang charisma.
Hindi sasagot diyan ang galing magsalita.
Tanging intimacy lang kay Jesus.
Sa John 15, paulit-ulit sinabi ni Jesus:
“Abide in Me.”
Ang Greek word na “abide” ay:
μένω (menō)
Ibig sabihin:
• manatili • manahan • manatiling konektado
Ang bunga ay hindi nanggagaling sa sobrang pagtakbo.
Nanggagaling ito sa pananatili kay Cristo.
Maraming believers ngayon ang burned out.
Hindi dahil kulang sila sa activity.
Kundi dahil mas mabilis silang tumatakbo kaysa manalangin. Mas mabilis mag-post kaysa makinig sa Diyos. Mas mabilis magsalita kaysa magsisi.
At eventually… bumabagsak ang kaluluwa.
Ang Diyos ay Mas Concerned sa Faithfulness Kaysa Fame
Napakaraming gustong mapansin.
Kahit spiritually.
Pero paulit-ulit sa Biblia:
Ginagamit ng Diyos ang mga taong hinubog sa lihim.
Si David nasa pastulan. Si Moises nasa disyerto. Si Elijah nasa brook. Si John the Baptist nasa wilderness.
Maging si Jesus…
Thirty years hidden.
Bago three years public ministry.
Hindi parusa ang hidden season.
Minsan preparation iyon.
Ang Hebrew word na:
כָּבוֹד (kavod)
na madalas isalin bilang “glory,” ay may idea ng:
• bigat • substance • spiritual weight
Ang tunay na authority may bigat.
Hindi puro hype. Hindi puro ingay. Hindi puro aesthetics.
At ang bigat na iyon…
nabubuo sa secret place.
Hindi sa clout.
Baka Kaya Ka Pinapabagal ng Diyos
May mga nagbabasa nito ngayon na feeling left behind.
Pakiramdam mo delayed ka. Hindi napapansin. Hindi ginagamit.
Pero baka proteksyon iyon.
Baka mahal ka ng Diyos para hayaang mauna ang platform kaysa character.
Baka ang katahimikan ay mercy.
Baka ang delay ay paghahanda.
Dahil kapag binigyan ka ng microphone nang hindi pa handa ang puso mo…
maaari kang masira.
At minsan ang pinakamalaking biyaya ay hindi acceleration.
Kundi formation.
Hindi Dumating si Jesus Para Magmukha Ka Lang Buhay
Maraming tao ang mukhang spiritually alive sa labas.
Pero patay na patay na sa loob.
Ngumingiti publicly. Umiiyak privately.
Nagpo-post ng verse. Pero gabi-gabing wasak.
Pero hindi dumating si Jesus para gumawa lang ng religious performers.
Dumating Siya para bumuhay ng patay na puso.
Ang salitang “repent” sa Greek ay:
μετανοέω (metanoeō)
Ibig sabihin:
• pagbabago ng isip • pagbabago ng direksyon • inward transformation
Ang Christianity ay hindi simpleng behavior modification.
Ito ay death and resurrection.
At baka may nagbabasa nito ngayon na sobrang pagod na.
Hindi physically.
Spiritually.
Pagod nang magpanggap. Pagod nang maging “okay.” Pagod nang tumakbo.
Ito ang paalala mo:
Hindi ka hinihingan ni Jesus ng performance.
Hinihingan ka Niya ng surrender.
At may awa pa rin para sa mga pagod na runner.
Hindi Tapos ang Diyos sa Iyo
Si Pedro bumagsak. Si Tomas nagduda. Si Jonas tumakbo. Si David nagkasala.
Pero hinabol pa rin sila ng biyaya ng Diyos.
Iyan ang Gospel.
Hindi lang tayo ine-expose ni Jesus.
Nire-restore Niya tayo.
At baka kaya tumama ito nang ganito kalalim…
Dahil alam mo ang pakiramdam ng tumatakbo habang ubos na ubos na sa loob.
At baka ngayon…
Tinatawag ka ni Jesus pabalik.
Hindi sa performance.
Kundi sa relationship.
Sa katotohanan. Sa pahinga. Sa Kanya.
Maging totoo ka.
Tinamaan ka nito, hindi ba?
May mga taong ngumiting okay sa labas habang unti-unti nang bumabagsak sa loob.
Kailangan nilang marinig ito.
May mga taong hindi pagod dahil kulang ang ginagawa nila.
Pagod sila dahil tumatakbo silang walang dalang kayang punuin lang ng presensya ni Jesus.
